dedupe_keys.name: grid interconnection as an upstream schedule constraint in data center delivery evidence from u s generation queues analysis code and data

description: Anh Chau and Carolina Esterellas Hernandez publish code and public inputs for studying grid interconnection as a data-centre delivery constraint. Zenodo lists an MIT-licensed archive and a machine-readable planning CSV; the repository README describes 26,695 United States interconnection requests filed from 2000 to 2025. Analyses include competing-risks survival models, duration models and machine learning, with a companion planning grid. These data can inform schedule-delay scenarios in digital and electricity-infrastructure simulations. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this assembled queue and delivery-risk package. Coverage is U.S. generation interconnection requests, not a direct census of data-centre connection applications. A limitation is that inferring a data-centre delivery delay from queue behaviour requires assumptions about project linkage. The manuscript is under review; Zenodo and GitHub name different target journals, so publication status is uncertain. Third-party public inputs retain source terms. No archive or CSV was downloaded and no hazard estimate was recalculated.
